text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: Elevated egress failures in us-west-2b for VPC vpc-0a1b2c3. Affected subnets: subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb. Pager: Priya K. Runbook: vpc-egress-checks.
Priya K: ack — I'm on it. looking at CW now.
Maria G: graph: https://metrics.internal/redwood/vpc/egress?start=1748205000 spike at ~14:11 UTC, error rate from NAT translations ~80%.
Alex P: any recent infra changes?
deploy-bot: CI deploy: Terraform apply completed by Infra CI at 2025-12-01T14:07:03Z — PR #345 merged (vpc: route-table associations).
Priya K: hmm. I see many ENIs reporting "no route" in VPC flow logs. snippet: `2025-12-01T14:11:18Z eni-0f.. 10.10.5.24 0.0.0.0 443 REJECT`
Jamie S: putting quick checklist: 1) check route-table associations for the private subnets 2) confirm NAT gateway attachments 3) run canary egress from SSM.
Alex P: pulling route tables now. `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3 --query 'RouteTables[*].{Id:RouteTableId,Associations:Associations}'`
Maria G: rtb-priv-old used to be associated with subnet-aaa & subnet-bbb — looks like association removed at 14:07.
Priya K: that aligns with the TF apply time. possible accidental removal of route_table_association block. can we re-associate?
Alex P: trying quick aws CLI re-associate to restore egress: `aws ec2 associate-route-table --subnet-id subnet-aaa --route-table-id rtb-priv-old` -> association a-0cdef123 created. doing subnet-bbb next.
Infra CI: FYI the PR changed modules/vpc/associations.tf removing explicit association to rtb-priv-old as part of refactor (author: infra-bob).
Jamie S: SSM canary: `aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-0a1b2c3 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters commands=["curl -sS --connect-timeout 5 https://ifconfig.me || echo FAIL"]`
Priya K: canary from i-0a1b2c3 returned success after re-assoc. public ip 3.12.45.99. NAT translations resumed.
Alex P: NAT gateway check: nat-0ff2a exists and healthy in subnet-public-1, but routes for private subnets were pointing to no target because of missing association.
Maria G: customer impact summary so far: ~18 minutes of egress failure for hosts in those two private subnets. Services behind them: batch workers + webhooks. Estimated failed requests ~1.2k. No data loss, just retries/timeouts.
Priya K: rolling rollback of the TF change in progress — reverting PR #345 and re-applying with explicit associations. running `terraform apply -target=module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.assoc_subnet_aaa -target=module.vpc.aws_route_table_association.assoc_subnet_bbb` to be surgical.
deploy-bot: Terraform apply started by Priya K at 2025-12-01T14:25:10Z. plan shows re-created associations only.
Alex P: after reapply, confirmed both subnets are associated with rtb-priv-old and routes show `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0ff2a`.
Jamie S: monitoring latency and error rates — graphs trending back to baseline.
Maria G: CloudWatch: Egress health metric back to nominal at 14:29 UTC. error rate dropped from 78% -> 1.5% within ~4 minutes of association.
Priya K: patch/followups: 1) revert PR #345 fully and rework associations in branch 2) add TF plan guard to flag removal of explicit private subnet associations 3) add a tiny smoke test in CI that runs a canary curl to ifconfig.me for infra changes touching VPCs 4) postmortem assign.
Alex P: adding temporary detection alert: if route-table association goes from associated->disassociated for prod subnets, fire high-priority pager.
Infra CI: noted — will add safety check to PR template and require two approvals for anything touching vpc.associations.
opsbot: Incident timeline created: https://incidents.internal/INC-2025-1221-01 (assigned to Priya K).
Priya K: handing off to Alex P for the post-incident writeup and long-term fixes. I'm OOO after 15:00 UTC, Alex you have the pager.
Alex P: got it, taking the handoff. I'll coordinate with infra-bob on the PR rewrite and schedule a retro.
Maria G: customer comms: status page updated: "Partial egress disruption in us-west-2 resolved. Some API calls may have failed between 14:07-14:25 UTC. Root cause: accidental removal of route table associations during infra refactor. Follow-up: improved PR checks and smoke tests."
Priya K: tagging SRE retrospective and assigning action items: @Alex P (lead), @Infra CI (safety checks), @Jamie S (smoke test), @Maria G (customer comm).
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved — services healthy. Duration ~22m.
Alex P: quick note — NAT gateway itself was fine; this was a routing-association regression. we'll add an automated read-before-apply check to detect orphaned private subnets in future.
Jamie S: also filing a runbook update to include immediate `associate-route-table` quick steps and the TF command to surgically reapply associations.
Priya K: thanks team. closing the loop. :thumbsup:
